Zmajevac Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zmajevac, Croatia

Not demolished. Zmajevac (historically Vörösmart), a Baranja village with Roman-era origins, developed a winemaking and fruit-production economy under mixed Hungarian-German settlement from the early 18th century, when Jewish settlers also arrived alongside the founding of both a synagogue and this cemetery. The community dissolved in 1914 at the start of WWI, its synagogue later sold in 1950. Zmajevac's most notable Jewish resident was Otti Berger (1898-1944), a celebrated Bauhaus textile designer who headed the movement's Weaving Workshop starting in 1931 before Nazi Germany barred her from working there in 1936 due to her Jewish heritage; she returned to Zmajevac in 1938 but was deported to Auschwitz with her family in April 1944, where she perished. This cemetery's tombstones span 1886 to 1941.
